headline: Issued Order of Conditions for dune fencing at 11 & 13 Bay View Avenue; continued 240 Lothrop Street ADU hearing to October 27, 2026.
summary: Members approved tree removals at 1025 Hale Street and 0 Longham Road, and issued a Negative 3 Determination for sewer and conduit work at 0 Trask Lane. They issued an Order of Conditions for dune fencing at 11 & 13 Bay View Avenue and continued the 240 Lothrop Street accessory dwelling unit hearing to October 27, 2026.
decisions: Approved tree removal request at 1025 Hale Street, 6-0.
Approved removal of four oak trees at 0 Longham Road, 6-0.
Continued the 240 Lothrop Street hearing to October 27, 2026, 6-0.
Issued a Negative 3 Determination of Applicability for sewer and electric conduit work at 0 Trask Lane with conditions, 6-0.
Lifted the Enforcement Order for 11 & 13 Bay View Avenue, 4-0-2 (Redmond and Power ineligible to vote).
Amended the Enforcement Order for 25 Linden Avenue to require attendance at the October 27, 2026 meeting after a site visit, 6-0.
Lifted the Enforcement Order for 23 Thoreau Circle, 6-0.
Lifted the Enforcement Order for 1 Brookwood Road, 6-0.
Approved payment of $22.58 for Conservation Agent August mileage and $32.56 for Conservation Field Inspector August mileage, 6-0.
Issued an Order of Conditions for dune fencing at 11 & 13 Bay View Avenue with special conditions, 4-0-2 (Redmond and Power ineligible to vote).
Approved the September 15, 2026 meeting minutes as amended, 5-0-1 (Power abstained).

 a.  Tree Removals 21 
   i.  New: 1025 Hale Street 22 
 23 
Dennis Silvio, Iron Tree Service, explains that there are four trees proposed to be removed from 24 
the property. There is one large white pine that is rotting away, a white oak that is choked with 25 
vines, a pear tree in decline, and a red oak split leader tree. These are being considered hazard 26 
trees. The trees are approximately 75’ from the wetlands. The proposal is to cut these flush to 27 
grade. The applicant plans to plant new trees and smaller bushes in the same area of the site. 28 
White agrees that these are hazard trees to the infrastructure on the property.  29 
 30 
Buchsbaum:  Motion to approve the tree removal request at 1025 Hale Street, with the 31 
conditions as discussed. Redmond seconds. Bertoni takes a roll call vote. Motion 32 
carries (6-0). 33 
 34 
   ii.  New: 0 Longham Road 35 
  36 
Nathan Mousseau, representing the Salem-Beverly Water Supply Board, explains that there is a 37 
new groundwater transmission main being installed on this property to be in compliance with 38 
current regulations. In order to install the meter vault, four oak trees are proposed to be removed 39 
as they will be severely undermined during excavation and could become hazardous. A certified 40 
arborist was not consulted for this work as the project is already behind schedule. The contractor 41 
identified the trees as problematic and hazardous to the project. The root structures for the trees 42 
may also need to be removed.  43 
 44

Buchsbaum suggests that this could have been addressed through an Amendment or Minor 45

this project to move forward. She suggests a retroactive filing for a Minor Modification to have it 48

 56

call vote. Motion carries (6-0). 58

4.  Notices of Intent/Abbreviated Notices of Intent/Requests for Amended Orders of 60 
Conditions/Abbreviated Notices of Resource Area Delineations 61 
a. Cont.: 11 & 13 Bay View Avenue, DEP File #5-1478 – install and maintain 62 
dune fencing – Kenyon Kellogg 63 
 64 
It is noted that Redmond and Power are not eligible to vote on this item. 65 
 66 
Bob Griffin, on behalf of the applicant, explains that this is a dune fencing project that was 67 
originally presented in August. A site walk was held on September 19, 2026 and there was no 68 
request for any plan changes. Dune fencing is proposed to be installed in the same areas as in 69 
recent years has been required via an Enforcement Order. There will be signs placed along the 70 
fence. All work will be completed by hand. The areas of fencing and signage seem to be 71 
protecting the dune well. In the winter, fencing in front of the dune is removed due to concerns 72 
about wave action. The fencing is proposed to be installed in April or May and removed in 73 
September. There is no phragmites removal proposed as part of this project. There are existing 74 
posts perpendicular to the shoreline. If these are deteriorated and need to be replaced, this work 75 
will be done by hand. Additional posts will be added to support the dune fence. There is an 76 
existing post that the fabric will tie to in order to terminate the fencing.  77 
 78 
Bertoni suggests that the number of posts be laid out for the preconstruction site visit. Fewer 79 
posts would be preferred. She notes that all of this area is above mean high water. 80 
 81 
Redmond asks how it will be determined when the fencing can be removed. Griffin explains that 82 
the Order of Conditions will typically be good for three years with the possibility of two one-83 
year extensions.  84 
 85 
Bertoni states that notice should be given to staff if the posts on either side of the stream need to 86 
be removed or relocated. Squibb states that he believes posts 15’ on center should suffice. Griffin 87 
disagrees and states that 8’-10’ would be preferred. Bertoni suggest 10’ spacing. 88 
 89
City of Beverly Conservation Commission  
October 6, 2026  
  Meeting Minutes  
 
Page 3 of 8 
 
There is no public comment. 90 
 91 
Buchsbaum:  Motion to close the hearing for 11 & 13 Bay View Avenue, DEP File #5-1478. 92 
Miller seconds. Bertoni takes a roll call vote. Motion carries (4-0-2, Redmond & 93 
Power are ineligible to vote). 94 
 95 
b. New: 240 Lothrop Street, No DEP File # as of posting – construct an 96 
Accessory Dwelling Unit and deck – Sean & Nicole Hartley 97 
 98 
Spidaliere reads the public legal notice. 99 
 100 
Mary Trudeau, representing the applicants, explains that this is an unusual property located 101 
between two streets. It fronts on Lothrop Street, and the back property line is bounded by Iverson 102 
Road. Beneath Iverson Road there is a flow which is believed to be primarily stormwater, 103 
although it could have also captured small streams in the area. It seems to emerge from the 104 
roadway into a well-defined channel that bisects this property. The applicants would like to 105 
construct an accessory dwelling unit (ADU) on their property. The proposal is a 24’x24’ 106 
addition, detached but connected by a breezeway. The 13,000 s.f. lot does not leave a lot of 107 
options for the location of an ADU, nor does it provide any location that would keep the ADU 108 
out of the 50’ No Build Zone. Mitigation for this intrusion is proposed as revegetation of the 109 
bank of stream with a combination of woody shrubs. Currently, the bank is stable but there is 110 
lawn running right up to the bank. The stream is not considered perennial on USGS, nor is it 111 
shown as perennial when run through the Stream Stats application. It is intermittent in flow and 112 
likely runs better when the storm drain system is full. However, it does have a very well defined 113 
channel. The applicant has proposed erosion and sedimentation controls around the limit of 114 
work. A stone apron detail is included on the plan, but the intent is to use the existing driveway 115 
to access the rear of the house. The intention is to do the limited amount of earth work required 116 
by using the existing driveway. This is not a full foundation addition but is proposed on pilings 117 
in order to have the least intrusive addition possible. The plans include information on how to 118 
manage any dewatering, though it is unlikely any will be needed. There is not a floodplain 119 
associated with this property and the stream does not show up on the USGS despite having a 120 
fairly well defined footprint. The wetlands were flagged in the spring 2025.  121 
 122 
Bertoni notes that the shrubs proposed are within the 25’ No Disturb Zone and a mitigation plan 123 
for the bank should be submitted. She asks that additional information on the Stream Stats for 124 
this be presented for the next meeting. 125 
 126 
Bertoni asks for public comment. 127 
 128 
Steph McGowan, 246 Lothrop Street, expresses support for the project. She notes that the 129 
existing wetland on the site seems very robust and she does not believe the proposed project will 130 
have an impact. 131 
 132 
Darren Blyth, 238 Lothrop Street, asks for clarification on the size of the ADU. Trudeau states 133 
that she believes it will be 24’x24’ but she will look further into this. Blyth asks about 134

stormwater management as the stream floods regularly and the proposal seems to lead to a total 135 
of 93% of impermeable surface on the site. Bertoni explains that the ADU is proposed to be on 136 
piles and so there will be open land under it. Trudeau states that roof runoff is proposed to be 137 
discharged through roof leaders. Some infiltration could be proposed though there may be issues 138 
with the vertical separation to groundwater. A French drain around the perimeter of the drip line 139 
of the roof could be a solution. 140 
 141 
Spidaliere reads a comment letter from the residents of 236 Lothrop Street, Donald & Sugar 142 
Moca, which expresses opposition to any building permit that would allow a concrete foundation 143 
in a lowland area and within the setback to the brook. Bertoni notes that the building will be built 144 
on sonotube piles which is less invasive than a concrete foundation. Trudeau states that she will 145 
bring back the calculations for the volume of displacement proposed by the project footings. This 146 
is not bordering the resource of Land Subject to Flooding.  147

6. Requests for Determination of Applicability 160 
 a.  New: 0 Trask Lane – upgrade an existing sewer line and install new   161 
  underground electric conduits – Corcoran Trask Lane LLC 162 
 163 
Spidaliere reads the public legal notice. 164 
 165 
Miranda Siemasko, representing the applicant, explains that the larger Trask Lane project was 166 
approved by the Commission more than a year ago. After the Order of Conditions was issued, 167 
the project was before the Planning Board for several more months before the Board issued a site 168 
plan review. The final decision contained a significant number of conditions, not all of which 169 
had been anticipated during the initial filings. One of those items was that the Planning Board 170 
required a sewer upgrade that the applicant was not anticipating. Hancock Associates has done 171 
the work to prepare those plans, and the applicant is requesting their approval by way of an 172 
RDA. There are other conditions outstanding to the Planning Board's decision, such as the 173 
Conservation Restriction, associated with this project. She notes that the Essex County Greenbelt 174 
Association has agreed to be a co-holder of the Conservation Restriction with the City. All of the 175 
details are being worked out in a Memorandum of Agreement. The item before the Commission 176 
this evening is limited to utility work. The applicant anticipates temporary disturbances within 177 
the Trask Lane right of way as well as a 40’ wide utility easement that currently exists and holds 178 
the existing sewer. 179
City of Beverly Conservation Commission  
October 6, 2026  
  Meeting Minutes  
 
Page 5 of 8 
 
 180 
Joe Peznola, Hancock Associates, explains that the proposal is an upgrade to the City sewer 181 
system. The project deals with the existing sewer that is currently being utilized by the various 182 
properties on Trask Lane and Colgate Road. The plans show a new sewer that is within the 183 
project limits, and which is still subject to the Planning Board approval and the Order of 184 
Conditions for the master project. This is being done separately because it impacts other 185 
properties, namely the Foley Hill apartments and the City of Beverly parcel. There is also work 186 
proposed within the City streets. There is an existing 8” line that runs down Trask Lane in a 187 
northerly direction until it gets to the back of the Folly Hill apartments. The intention is to cut the 188 
trench, remove the existing 8” pipe, and replace it with a 12” pipe, while retaining the existing 189 
core for the new 12” pipe so that it will be at the same elevation as the 8” pipe. A new electric 190 
conduit will run parallel to this. The applicant also did not anticipate a major upgrade needed to 191 
the electrical service for the area. National Grid needs to bring new wires and new power 192 
because the existing service and lines are not sufficient to power the new project and continue to 193 
service the area. Behind the Folly Hill apartments there is an existing 40’ easement in a 194 
landscaped area. There is a small area that goes into the 25’ No Disturb Zone within Trask Lane. 195 
As some of the existing sewer line runs under the wetlands, the applicant is proposing to relocate 196 
that portion of the line, pull the manholes on either side of it which are outside of the wetlands, 197 
plug the pipe, and leave the pipe abandoned in place so as not to disturb the wetland. Thus, only 198 
buffer zone work is proposed, and the applicant is eliminating any future need to go into the 199 
wetlands. 200 
 201 
Peznola explains that the easement then crosses onto the Trask Lane property and runs down an 202 
existing walking path. There is not a lot of vegetation that will be disturbed in this area. All of 203 
the work in this area will also be within buffer zone with the same notion of maintaining the 204 
manholes, trenching, replacing with a 12” pipe, and back filling. There will be some bypass 205 
pumping needed. Correspondence from the Engineering Department was received requiring a 206 
temporary sewer bypass plan and a dewatering plan. The bypass pumping will be handled at each 207 
manhole segment. There will be generators on site with alarms for temporary power should 208 
anything go wrong so that pumping can continue. Whenever possible, the applicant will utilize 209 
the existing pipe network to pump into, and this language can be included in the plan. In terms of 210 
the dewatering, there is limited space so there will be long linear filter bags alongside the work 211 
area. There will be constant inspections from the City Engineering Department and Public Works 212 
Department. There will be communication between the departments and Commission staff. 213 
Other than removal of some saplings that should not be in the easement anyway, there is no tree 214 
removal proposed. 215 
 216 
Bertoni states that the plan mentions tree removal within 10’ of the sewer line prior to 217 
replacement. She asks if this will be flagged. Peznola states that the erosion control line will be 218 
very controlled and there will only be selective brush cutting allowed. The entire erosion control 219 
will be laid down prior to the start of work, and the work will then be done in sections. 220 
 221 
Buchsbaum asks about restoration of the areas outside of the 10’ area to be cleared within the 222 
easement. Peznola states that the lawn areas will be seeded and the walking path areas could be 223 
seeded with a wetland mix if needed.  224

 262

9. Orders of Conditions, If Any  286 
a. 11 & 13 Bay View Avenue, DEP File #5-1478 – install and maintain dune 287 
fencing – Kenyon Kellogg 288 
 289 
It is noted that Redmond and Power are not eligible to participate in this item. 290 
 291 
The Commission reviews a draft Order of Conditions, including the following special conditions 292 
(under the Act and the Ordinance), in addition to the standard general and perpetual conditions: 293 
1. The Intermittent Stream channel shall not be blocked by dune fencing.  294 
  Dune fencing posts and rope shall be monitored and shifted to ensure that  295 
  the channel is not blocked. This condition shall survive in perpetuity  296 
  beyond the issuance of a Certificate of Compliance. 297 
2. Further alteration within the dune grass mitigation area is prohibited,  298 
  except as may be required to maintain the area in its mitigated condition,  299 
  such as planting dune grass. This condition shall survive in perpetuity  300 
  beyond the issuance of a Certificate of Compliance. 301 
3. The fencing shall be installed no earlier than April 1st and shall be   302 
  removed no later than September 30th on an annual basis for the life of this 303 
  Order of Conditions. 304 
4. If the posts need to be moved due to changes in the Intermittent Stream  305 
  channel, the homeowner shall contact the Conservation Agent to   306 
  determine if a formal filing with the Conservation Commission is   307 
  required. 308 
5. The fencing shall be removed at the expiration of the Order of Conditions. 309 
 310
